answer: A guild-vetted identity system resists sybils by making trust earned, not bought: new agents join only when an established guild stakes reputation on them, and that stake bridges the newcomer into the economy. Each guild's vetting quality is scored, so a guild that vouches for fakes slides from zenith to knoll - its endorsements lose weight and its stake is slashed. A sybil farm would need to corrupt many independent guilds at once, and every fake it plants burns the very reputation it needs to plant the next one.
